items.title: What you see, what you don’t
Public transport stories
items.summary: The evidence tells us that many deaf people and people with hearing loss have to navigate barriers that most passengers never have to think about when using public transport. Here, we show how what those barriers are like in practice, with two stories from Sarah and Charlotte.

items.title: Policy statement: Transport
items.summary: RNID uses evidence to inform our work to change the lives of individuals, systems and services, and society and public attitudes.

items.title: Bibliography
items.summary: Academic references Aarhaug, J., & Elvebakk, B. (2015). The impact of Universally accessible public transport–a before and after study . Transport Policy, 44 , 143–150. Almoshaogeh, M., Jamal, A., Ahmed, T., Alharbi, F., Iqbal, M., Haider, H., & Alinizzi, M. (2025).

items.title: Conclusions and future research
items.summary: This review has identified a range of barriers and enablers of access for deaf people and people with hearing loss when they use public transport. These relate to systems and infrastructure, information and communication, and attitudes and awareness.

items.title: Impacts
items.summary: This section analyses the impact of the problems discussed in the previous sections. Access problems and negative experiences with public transport can have both emotional impacts such as reduced confidence, and practical impacts such as difficulty planning and making journeys.

items.title: Enabling access to public transport
items.summary: Most of the research reviewed identified problems preventing access to public transport. However, there were examples of how systems and infrastructure, information and communication, and attitudes and awareness can instead support access.

items.title: Attitudes and awareness
items.summary: The final theme relates to social aspects of accessibility, such as the attitudes and awareness of transport staff and the public.

items.title: Information and communication
items.summary: Access to information is essential for using public transport, including finding and understanding timetables, buying tickets, and accessing real-time information while travelling. Deaf people and people with hearing loss cannot access this information when it is provided solely in audio format.

items.title: Systems and infrastructure
items.summary: The theme of systems and infrastructure includes parts of the transport system such as the design of train carriages and the layout of stations, how well legislation is enforced, and how easy and effective it is to make a complaint.
